Product Menu

The full-width product header: brand lockup, main navigation, Search and Ask AI utilities, and the primary call-to-action. A second variant adds a sub-navigation tier for documentation-heavy sections.

2 variants72px + 65px tiersFigma 790:4778

Default

One 72px tier. The standard product navigation bar with brand logo, main top-menu links, Search and Ask AI utility options, and the “Start for Free” CTA.

variant="default"

With sub menu

Adds a 65px second tier below the main navigation. Best used to group detailed, page-specific resources like API references, code examples, tutorials and licensing options. The lead chip is the current page; showMenuItems2 appends a divided trailing group at the right end.

Responsive

Same as Top Nav: the Figma canvas is 1440 desktop only, so everything below it is an implementation decision. This one sheds in three steps — the runtime badge below 1180, the utilities below 1024, and the centre group below 768, after which the menu and the sub-menu scroll sideways instead of wrapping.
The preview is an <iframe> loading this same page at ?frame=, because an iframe is the only box on a page with a viewport of its own — the demo frames above are pinned to 1440 by .frame-scroll and will never show this. Nothing is duplicated to make it work.
1024px
Only 1024 and 768 of those three are on the project’s breakpoint scale; 1180 is not. Drag across each to see what goes. The horizontal scroll below 1024 is deliberate — a nav that wraps to two rows moves everything under it, which is worse than one that scrolls. The handle takes arrow keys (±16, or ±1 with Shift), which is the only reliable way to land on an exact threshold.

Code

// default — one tier
<ProductMenu
  product="pdf" productName="PDF"
  items={[
    { label: 'Home', active: true },
    { label: 'Licensing', href: '/licensing' },
    { label: 'Features' },
    { label: 'Demos' },
    { label: 'Docs' },
  ]}
/>

// with the sub tier
<ProductMenu
  variant="submenu"
  items={items}
  subLead={{ label: 'Get Started' }}
  subItems={[{ label: 'Tutorials' }, { label: 'API Reference' }]}
  showMenuItems2
  subItemsTrailing={[{ label: 'Licensing' }]}
/>

// bare bar — no runtime label, no utilities, custom CTA
<ProductMenu product="ocr" productName="OCR" runtime=""
  showSearch={false} showAskAi={false} ctaLabel="Get a licence" items={items} />
<nav class="pm" aria-label="Product">
  <div class="pm-bar">
    <a class="pm-brand" href="/">
      <img class="pm-mark" src="assets/mark-pdf.svg" alt="" width="40" height="40">
      <span class="pm-name"><b>IRON</b><span class="pm-name-hl">PDF</span></span>
      <span class="pm-runtime">for .NET</span>
    </a>
    <div class="pm-center">
      <ul class="pm-menu">
        <li><a class="pm-item is-active" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
        <li><a class="pm-item">Licensing <svg class="pm-caret">…</svg></a></li>
      </ul>
      <div class="pm-utils">
        <button class="pm-util" aria-label="Search">…</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="pm-right"><a class="pm-cta">Start for Free</a></div>
  </div>
</nav>

Guidelines

From Figma’s own Do & Don’t sheet for this component (node 801:3737).
✓ Do
  • Use the submenu variant when linking deep, documentation-heavy subcategories, to prevent main-tier clutter.
  • Keep the primary download call-to-action consistently visible at the right-most end to capture key traffic.
  • Leverage the Search and Ask AI bubbles to aid quick, exploratory, keyboard-driven site discovery.
✗ Don't
  • Don’t stack more than five primary options in the centre group — smaller viewports need the breathing space.
  • Don’t hide the dropdown carets when an item opens sub-options; that removes the visual signpost.
  • Don’t use high-contrast accents inside the secondary bar — submenus keep a muted status hierarchy.

Notes

Figma specifies this component at 1440px desktop only — its guidelines talk about “desktop screen breakpoints” and there is no mobile frame. The narrow-viewport behaviour here (drop the runtime label at 1180px, the utility bubbles at 1024px, then the whole centre group at 768px, with both tiers scrolling horizontally) is an implementation decision, not a handed-over design.

The 40px brand mark is Figma’s own size in this bar. It is deliberately off the 24/48/96/192 grid documented on the Logo page, so it is set explicitly here rather than going through the Logo component’s typed size.
